title: The release commit carries a declared trailer, so it ends with the house (C) line in every project
body:
The release commit carries a declared trailer, so a project's release commit meets the house commit rule.

## The gap

The core commits the release commit with `--only` and `-m "release: $tag"` and no body (`lib/cmd/release:2809`). So every project cutting through the core gets a one-line release commit, devbin's own included: `be40dea7`, devbin 0.1.20's release commit, reads exactly `release: v0.1.20`.

The house rule is that a commit message ends with the maintainer's `(C)` line. A machine-made commit is still a commit in the history, so the core's release commit falls short of it in every project at once. Intent's driver works around it by adding the line itself as a second paragraph, which is a local patch of a core behaviour, and the kind of divergence that drifts.

## The ask

A declared trailer, appended to the release commit's message as a second paragraph. The subject stays `release: <tag>`, so the tag readers, `release status`, `release_commit` and the formula are untouched.

Devbin declares its own with the rest, so devbin's next release commit carries the line, and Intent drops its driver's addition.

## Where it came from

Raised by intent-vc on 2026-11-10 out of Intent's ST0091 WP-01 re-inventory, and measured here against devbin's own release commit. hv ruled the same day: the core takes the declared trailer, one shape for every project.

## Resolution

Fixed in one landing on main, 8f5c7d44caa610139e69253a05d3fb2f4802c196 (2026-11-10 16:52Z), from the tested tip 9adb8b3d, unpushed until devbin's next cut, proved on its own arms under hv's rule of 2026-11-05 (red at the base's code, green at the fix) in one slot on devbin-vc's desk.

- `release.trailer`, a list of lines, read once by the cut. Where it is declared the commit step hands git a second -m with its lines, so the release commit's message is `release: <tag>`, a blank line, then the lines in order; the subject is unchanged, declared or not. The dry run's commit row and the done row name the trailer and its line count.
- A trailer line holding a skip marker is refused as config, in any case, through cfg_ci_skip_marker, as `release.snapshot.message`'s are, since the release commit is what CI is read on wherever `release.publish.url` is not declared.
- devbin's own config declares its trailer, `(C) hello@matthewsinclair.com`, so its next release commit ends as every commit in the repository does.
- The config reader, on devbin-vc's ruling: a list item quoted whole is one scalar, whatever it holds. The reader refused any item holding ": " as a sequence of maps, quoted or not, against its own grammar, so no trailer line of git's `Key: value` shape could be declared. `quoted_scalar` takes an item as a quoted scalar only when its opening quote closes at its end and nowhere before it, so a bare `k: v` and a quoted key with its value, `"k": "v"`, are still refused. Nothing that read before reads otherwise; it was checked under BSD awk and mawk.
- docs/configuration.md gains the trailer's row, its place in the skip-marker rule and a sentence under the grammar table; lib/pages/release.md's commit row, docs/releasing.md's step 3 and the reference config say what the commit carries.

Six new arms: three in releasecut.bats (the message with a two-line trailer and its commit row, the dry run's row, and the subject alone when none is declared), one in releasecore.bats (a marker refused, the same line without it accepted) and two in config.bats (a quoted item holding ": " read as its text in either quote, and a quoted key with its value still refused). Four were red at the base, the quoted-item arm on its own assertion, the two trailer arms at the base reader's refusal the unit answers and the marker arm at the base's unknown key; the two that hold behaviour the base already has were green there by construction, as declared before the run. 38 green legs, the six with the commit step, the subject's readers, the release table's arms, the docs ties, the arms reading devbin's own config, the release-table walkers and the reader's own arms, were green at the fix. Intent drops its driver's own (C) line once devbin's next release is swept into it.
